content: Chest radiographs, commonly referred to as chest x-rays, are radiographic images of the chest that are utilized in medical practice to diagnose conditions affecting the lungs. Digital chest radiographs, in particular, are employed for both diagnostic purposes and for medical screening and surveillance of lung health. A B Reader is a physician who has undergone specialized training and certification to interpret and classify chest x-ray findings specifically related to pneumoconiosis, a group of lung diseases caused by the inhalation of mineral dust. Chest radiography plays a critical role in the early detection of pneumoconioses, which are lung diseases induced by dust exposure. Early identification of affected workers allows for timely interventions aimed at reducing or eliminating further exposure to harmful dust, thereby decreasing the likelihood of disease progression. Radiographic images of individuals exposed to mineral dust are systematically classified by B Readers in accordance with the International Labour Office (ILO) International Classification of Radiographs of Pneumoconioses. This classification system is the most widely recognized and standardized method for assessing the presence and severity of pneumoconiosis in chest radiographs. The data derived from these classifications are utilized by government programs and public health agencies globally to analyze the appearance and epidemiology of pneumoconiosis, contributing to a better understanding of the disease and its impact. To ensure the effective use of chest radiographs, it is essential to maintain ongoing attention to the personnel, equipment, and procedures involved in the imaging process. The document titled Application of Digital Radiography for the Detection and Classification of Pneumoconiosis provides detailed guidance and recommendations for obtaining high-quality digital images that can be used for the accurate classification of pneumoconiosis findings.
